finalText:
All 4 tests pass.

## Root cause

`src/jobs/processOrder.js` acquired a connection with `pool.acquire()` and only released it *after* `await run(conn, order)` succeeded — no try/finally. Every rejected order (bad payload) permanently leaked that connection, since the pool has no timeout-based reclaim (by design, per `pool.js`'s comment).

The logs confirm it exactly:
- Each `invalid order payload` failure in `worker.log` (starting with order-4013 at 01:56:11) has no corresponding "connection released" line, unlike every successful job.
- After enough leaks accumulated, the pool hit exhaustion at order-4126 (02:06:33).
- That cascaded into a full outage at 02:11+, with `api`, `worker-2`, and `scheduler` all failing on `pool exhausted` / `acquire timeout` — the 2am page.

## Fix

Rewrote `processOrder` to use the existing `withConnection` safe wrapper (the same one `handlers/api.js` already uses) instead of duplicating manual acquire/release:

```js
async function processOrder(pool, order, run) {
  return withConnection(pool, (conn) => run(conn, order));
}
```

This guarantees release via `finally`, matching the pattern the tests expect. All 4 tests in `tests/pool.test.js` pass now (they were red before because the leak-under-failure and concurrent-failure cases exhausted the pool).
